title: receiveTypingIndicators unenforced for channel Chats in mailbox-per-user topology
description:
In the mailbox-per-user topology (spec Section 1.1), each participant runs their own JMAP server storing only their own data. Channel Chats exist within a Space, which lives on the Space-owning server. The spec does not specify whether channel Chat records are replicated to each member's home server in this topology — federation replication rules are deferred to JMAP-CHAT-FED.

receiveTypingIndicators is an owner-side preference checked by the server before delivering a typing event. In the mailbox-per-user topology, the server that would deliver a typing event to a member is that member's home server. If no channel Chat record exists on the member's home server (because the channel lives on the Space-owning server), then the home server has no Chat record to check, and the preference cannot be enforced.

In the relay topology this is not an issue: all members connect to the shared relay, which holds one Chat record per member per channel.

The spec must either:
(a) Require that channel Chat records be replicated to each member's home server (with the receiveTypingIndicators field), or
(b) Clarify that in the mailbox-per-user topology, typing event delivery and receiveTypingIndicators enforcement for channel Chats is the responsibility of the Space-owning server (which does hold the Chat record), or
(c) Explicitly exempt channel Chats from the receiveTypingIndicators requirement in the mailbox-per-user topology and document the gap.

Without one of these, a conforming mailbox-per-user implementation cannot enforce receiveTypingIndicators for channel Chats, creating a silent interoperability failure.

Relevant locations: draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00.md Chat object receiveTypingIndicators field (line 438); Chat/typing Server Behavior (line 904); Deployment Topologies section (lines 86-94).
close_reason: Fixed in review fix wave or recorded as accepted design decision.
